text:
linh: Hey team — our app started getting 300-500ms extra tail latency to Redwood endpoints this morning and I can see calls hitting eu-west-1 even though we set region=us-west-2 in the client. Any idea?

ana: Sorry about that, can you paste a sample request (headers + region setting)? Is this happening for all keys or a few users?

linh: Sample: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX\" -H \"X-Region: us-west-2\" -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-13b\",\"prompt\":\"hello\"}'`
Only started ~09:15 UTC, affects ~20% of our traffic.

mike-sre: Noted. Checking routing logs for that customer key now. Can you give me the request_id from a slow trace?

linh: One trace: `req_0a7f9d`. Hit eu-west-1

deploy-bot: Rollout: failover-policy-service v2.4.1 deployed at 1802523000 by @ci.

ana: @mike-sre looks like this lines up with the rollout window. Mike, any obvious config issues?

mike-sre: Pulled the active failover policies for that org. Here's the rules blob (sanitized):
```json
{"failover": [{"region":"us-west-2","priority":2,"weight":"10","sticky":true},{"region":"eu-west-1","priority":1,"weight":"0","sticky":false}], "global_sticky": true}
```

mike-sre: Uh. Note that eu-west-1 has priority 1 but weight 0 and sticky false — that seems wrong. Priority numbers are lower=higher priority but a recent change inverted the sort when weights are strings.

ana: So traffic could be routed to eu-west-1 because the code compared priority as string and '1' > '2' lexicographically?

mike-sre: Exactly. The bug in v2.4.1 serializes weights/priorities as strings and then we do a string sort in the routing layer. If sticky routing is enabled global_sticky=true, a new sticky assignment ended up picking eu-west-1 for some customers.

linh: Is there a rollback we can do? High latency is hurting our SLAs.

josh-pm: We should either rollback the service or push a hotfix. What’s the blast radius? Which customers affected?

mike-sre: From logs: ~18% of requests for a subset of orgs hit eu-west-1 during 09:12–09:45 UTC. I can map org ids and put a list in the ticket.

ana: Immediate mitigation: disable global_sticky or mask the new failover-service version so routing uses previous behavior. Can we flip a feature flag?

mike-sre: I staged a config to coerce priority/weight fields to ints in the router as a hotfix and rolled it to 10% at 09:30. Telemetry shows affected orgs dropping to 2% after 09:40.

linh: Thanks — saw improvement around 09:42, much better now.

deploy-bot: Rollout: config-hotfix-int-coerce rolled to 100% at 1802523600 by @mike-sre

ana: Action items:
1) mike-sre: continue mapping affected orgs and notify account owners (in progress).
2) eng-runtime: revert v2.4.1 serialization or enforce numeric types at ingestion.
3) support: notify customers who reported SLAs and provide repro + mitigation steps.

mike-sre: Repro steps I used for engineering:
- POST requests with header `X-Region: us-west-2` and typical key set.
- Inspect failover decision logs: `curl https://admin.redwood/internal/failover?org=ORG_ID`
- Confirmed policy blob had string weights/priorities.
- Temporary cli to coerce: `jq '.failover[] |= (.priority |= tonumber) | (.weight |= tonumber)' policy.json`

josh-pm: I'll open an internal ticket with severity P1 and link traces + rollout window. We need a postmortem: why did serialization change slip past tests.

linh: Appreciate the quick response. Will reach out if anything else flares up.

ana: Thanks everyone. I'll draft a short customer note to send to affected customers and include the mitigation and ETA for a permanent fix. :white_check_mark:
